title: Property of the descended finite affine presentation
statement:
Every chart, overlap open, and overlap map in the constructed raw datum
base changes to its named counterpart in $\mathsf R_X$.

proof.text: Retain the fixed presentation and all the choices of [def-nagata-relative-gluing-datum-descent]. Let $F$ be its finite set of chosen stages and put $r=\lambda_{\mathrm{raw}}=u(F)$. By [lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound], each stage in $F$ is at most $r$. In particular every transported chart, overlap open and overlap morphism used below is defined at $r$. We use only these fixed choices, not independence of the lifts.

source.place: ## Proof; Stacks Tag 01ZM, limits.tex, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, proof of (1), stages i_2 through i_4

proof.text: Write $p_\lambda:S\to S_\lambda$ and $s_{\lambda r}:S_r\to S_\lambda$. For any chosen model $Z_\lambda\to S_\lambda$, the universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $(Z_\lambda\times_{S_\lambda}S_r)\times_{S_r}S$ with $Z_\lambda\times_{S_\lambda}S$: send a compatible triple $(z,t,s)$ to $(z,s)$, and send $(z,s)$ back to $(z,p_r(s),s)$. These formulas mean the unique morphisms with the indicated projections; they are well defined because $s_{\lambda r}p_r=p_\lambda$ by [def-nagata-basechanged-system], and their composites fix both projections, hence are identities. For a morphism $h:Z_\lambda\to T_\lambda$ over $S_\lambda$, either order of these identifications and base change has projections $h(z)$ and $s$; uniqueness therefore shows that the identification commutes with $h$. This proves the transport compatibility used in the next three steps directly from the universal property.

source.place: ## Proof; Stacks Tag 01ZM, limits.tex, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, proof of (1), stages i_2 through i_4

proof.text: For each chart algebra $B$, [lemma-nagata-affine-fp-descends] says that its chosen comparison $\beta_B:B_{\lambda_B}\otimes_{A_{\lambda_B}}A\to B$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the inverse of $\operatorname{Spec}(\beta_B)$ identifies the base-changed affine chart with the named chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ over the chosen base open. The raw chart at $r$ is precisely the base change of this chosen model, by [def-nagata-relative-gluing-datum-descent]. Applying Step 2 with $\lambda=\lambda_B$ gives its comparison with the same named chart. The projections in the cited affine fibre-product statement show that the comparison respects the structure map to the base chart.

proof.text: For each chosen overlap open $W$ in a chart, write $\omega$ for its own chosen descent stage (before the common overlap stage). [lemma-nagata-qc-open-descends] gives $p_{Y,\omega}^{-1}(W_{\omega})=W$. In the raw datum the later open is the inverse image $W_r=t_{r\omega}^{-1}(W_{\omega})$ under the chart transition $t_{r\omega}$, by [def-nagata-relative-gluing-datum-descent]. Compatibility of the chart projections gives $t_{r\omega}p_{Y,r}=p_{Y,\omega}$; hence $p_{Y,r}^{-1}(W_r)=p_{Y,\omega}^{-1}(W_{\omega})=W$ by composition of inverse images. The same two lines with $r$ replaced by any stage $v\geq\omega$ give $p_{Y,v}^{-1}(t_{v\omega}^{-1}(W_\omega))=W$; in particular this holds at the common overlap stage $w=\lambda_W$ used in Steps 6--8. This is the asserted recovery of the named open in the chart comparison of Step 3. Its open subscheme comparison is the restricted chart comparison, with the same projections as in Step 2.

source.place: ## Proof; Stacks Tag 01ZM, limits.tex, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, proof of (1), stages i_2 through i_4

proof.text: Let $w=\lambda_W$ be the common overlap stage. For every $v\geq\lambda_0$ needed below, the transition $S_v\to S_{\lambda_0}$ is affine by [def-nagata-relative-gluing-datum-descent], hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (3). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2) to this transition and the qcqs scheme $S_{\lambda_0}$. Thus $S_v$ is qcqs, in particular for $v=w$ and for each chart descent stage.

source.place: Tags 01KU(2) (lemma-separated-permanence), and lemma-composition-quasi-compact; affine input: Morphisms Tag 01S7 (lemma-affine-separated).

proof.text: Fix one overlap and let $\omega\leq w$ be its individual open-descent stage. Its chosen open $W_\omega$ is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-qc-open-descends]. The chart transition $C_w\to C_\omega$ is the pullback of $S_w\to S_\omega$: its projections are the maps of [def-nagata-basechanged-system], with the comparison of Step 2. It is affine, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (1),(3). The transported open is $W_w=(C_w\to C_\omega)^{-1}(W_\omega)$ by [def-nagata-relative-gluing-datum-descent]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open] makes $W_w$ quasi-compact. This argument applies to both source and target opens of every overlap map.

source.place: Tag 01K4 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine); affine base change: Morphisms Tag 01SD (lemma-base-change-affine).

proof.text: Fix a chart descent stage $b$. The base chart $V_b\subseteq S_b$ is the inverse image of its fixed affine base chart at $\lambda_0$, by [def-nagata-relative-gluing-datum-descent]. Its projection to that affine chart is a base change of the affine transition of bases, so $V_b$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (1),(2). The chosen chart is $\operatorname{Spec}B_b\to V_b$, where $B_b$ is finitely presented over the base-chart ring by [lemma-nagata-affine-fp-descends]. Step 5 gives qcqs of $S_b$ and $S_w$. Step 2 identifies its chart at $w$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B_b\times_{S_b}S_w$, and Step 6 gives quasi-compactness of its overlap open $W_w$. Apply [lem-nagata-qc-open-basechanged-affine-chart-fp] with $S=S_b$, $T=S_w$, $V=V_b$ and $B=B_b$. Every source and target overlap model is consequently of finite presentation over $S_w$.

For each named overlap morphism $\varphi$, use [lemma-nagata-morphism-descends] with initial index $w$. Its base is qcqs by Step 5, its two models are of finite presentation by Step 7, and its limit models are identified with the named overlaps by Steps 3 and 4. The fixed choices in [def-nagata-relative-gluing-datum-descent] are precisely the choices to which that property lemma applies. Hence the base change to $S$ of the chosen morphism at $\lambda_\varphi$ is the given $\varphi$. Apply this separately to both directions of each overlap isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), (2) and its use at i_4 in the proof of (1).

proof.text: By [def-nagata-relative-gluing-datum-descent], the raw map at $r$ is the base change of the chosen map at $\lambda_\varphi\leq r$. Apply the natural comparison already proved in Step 2 to that map: either composite to its target model has projections $\varphi_{\lambda_\varphi}(z)$ and $s$. Uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product] makes the two composites equal. Its further base change to $S$ is therefore the map of Step 8, hence $\varphi$, with exactly the chart and open comparisons of Steps 3 and 4.

proof.text: The raw datum consists exactly of these charts, overlap opens, and maps by [def-nagata-relative-gluing-datum-descent]. Steps 3, 4 and 9 thus give every component comparison in the statement. No gluing identity at the finite stage is needed for this conclusion.

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned long Step 5 without changing the statement, Lean record or Steps 1-4. Its hidden qcqs and transported-open compactness arguments now cite existing permanence statements in short steps. One statement-only lemma isolates finite presentation of quasi-compact opens in base changes of affine finitely presented charts. Morphism descent is applied with every hypothesis verified, followed by the elementary naturality comparison already established in Step 2. Corrected the retained attempt's unlogged search records by using real recorded queries and eliminated its redundant common-stage and transport nodes.

tool_uses.why: The generic fibre-product universal property gives the explicit inverse and naturality of iterated base change; no unit-specific theorem replaces this definition.
The affine tensor-product description converts the chart algebra comparison into the scheme comparison, with the specified projections; no Nagata-unit node states this generic fact.
Affineness under base change, affineness over an affine target and qcqs of an affine morphism are generic inputs to common-stage bookkeeping, not another approximation route.
Clause (2) propagates qcqs from the fixed initial base along affine transitions; no unit-local node states the generic permanence fact.
Inverse images under the affine chart transitions preserve compactness of the descended overlap opens; this generic topological permanence statement is not a change of approximation route.

Steps 1-10 hold. Step 2 (iterated base change through the fibre-product universal property) and Steps 9-10 really are elementary. Step 5 proves every base stage S_v is qcqs from affine-permanence (3) and qcqs-permanence (2). Step 6 shows W_w is quasi-compact: the chart transition is affine and a quasi-compact map pulls back quasi-compact opens. In Step 7 all hypotheses of the new lemma hold: S_b and S_w are qcqs, V_b is affine by affine-permanence (1),(2), B_b is finitely presented by affine-fp-descends, and the stage order b<=omega<=w is fixed by the definition. Step 8 matches Stacks 01ZM(2) exactly: S_w is qcqs and both overlap models are of finite presentation over it. The new node lem-nagata-qc-open-basechanged-affine-chart-fp is true, by the argument 01TQ, then 01TU for V into S, 01TR, 01TS, X_T qcqs, then 01TU for W into X_T, then 01TR. It holds in the small cases: W or T empty, B=A with t=id, and a non-affine W. It is statement-only and self-contained, and it does not restate a clause of the item. Searching the DAG with rg (01TQ/01TR/01TS/01TU, 'quasi-compact open immersion') found no duplicate: proper-fp-permanence (d), qcqs-morphism-permanence, qc-open-immersion-finite-type and lfp-composition each give only part of it. I accept the declared tool uses: three lem-weil-pbc permanence nodes, all with Mathlib status, plus the two already recorded. No SGA source is used and the target is not weakened. One fix: Step 4 proved the recovery of the named open only at stage r, but Step 8 uses it at the common overlap stage w. I added one sentence to Step 4 saying the same two-line computation holds at every stage v>=omega, in particular at w. proof.text:
Apply the corresponding property lemma to each finite-presentation chart,
quasi-compact overlap, and overlap morphism. There are only finitely many
objects, and the common upper bound transports all of them to one stage
without changing their base changes.
